analysis_type: High-precision joint coefficient support on fixed-period ellipsoid slices of the native ENSO Fourier model, with deterministic feasible period-perturbation tests against exporting those slice bounds to the full ellipsoid; no refitting, global optimizer claim or probability region

slice_rule.slice: For each fold, freeze b4 and b7 at their native centers and retain the seven-dimensional coefficient slice of the same nine-dimensional ellipsoid; no period estimate or covariance is changed
slice_rule.schur_complement: With c denoting the seven coefficients and p the two periods, use S=C_cc-C_cp*C_pp^(-1)*C_pc. This is the quadratic-form matrix of the ellipsoid slice, not the marginal coefficient block C_cc and not a posterior conditional covariance
slice_rule.support: At each held-out month, form v(x) from the intercept and actual sine/cosine values at the frozen center periods. Evaluate the center prediction f_c(x) with the original native model and compute f_c(x) plus or minus radius*sqrt(v(x)^T*S*v(x))
slice_rule.outward_rounding: Use 80-digit mpmath arithmetic, the frozen 1e-24 outward relative margin and nextafter outward conversion; this is a numerical interval certificate, not exact rational algebra
slice_rule.positive_definite_check: Require both C and S to be symmetric positive definite by high-precision Cholesky and fail rather than fabricate a bound
slice_rule.independent_comparison: Compare each slice envelope with the stage-47 independent-coefficient envelope at the same fold and month. The conditional slice envelope must be contained in that baseline envelope; report width ratio and width reduction
slice_rule.scope: The support is jointly optimized over the seven coefficients only on the fixed-period slice. It is not a joint nonlinear optimum over the full nine-dimensional ellipsoid

candidate_rule.direction_formula: For each period p and each sign, set theta_candidate=theta_center+sign*radius*sqrt(C_pp)*e_p, leaving every other parameter at its center. These four points lie on the full ellipsoid boundary by the support identity
candidate_rule.evaluation: Evaluate the original nonlinear Fourier model with each candidate's actual periods and every unique held-out month. Do not use fixed-period or Taylor substitution for the candidate evaluation
candidate_rule.feasibility: Recompute the full ellipsoid quadratic form for every candidate and require it to equal radius^2 within the high-precision numerical tolerance; require both candidate periods to remain strictly positive
candidate_rule.slice_violation: Record whenever a candidate prediction lies below the conditional slice lower bound or above its upper bound. Retain every candidate and every month, including zero-violation records
candidate_rule.independent_baseline_check: Require every candidate prediction to remain inside the stage-47 independent full-ellipsoid envelope at the same fold and month; this audits implementation consistency and is not a new independent validation
candidate_rule.not_optimizer: The four deterministic directions are feasibility witnesses only, not global maximizers or minimizers of the nonlinear model

outcome_rule.violation_witness: Any strictly outside candidate is a concrete counterexample to exporting the fixed-period slice bound to the full ellipsoid; record its direction, parameters, month, prediction and exceedance
outcome_rule.zero_witness: If no candidate violates a slice bound, report only that these four directions found no witness. Never infer full-ellipsoid safety from an empty candidate counterexample set
outcome_rule.tightening: Report conditional width reductions independently from full-region violation counts; a large slice tightening does not compensate for a full-region counterexample
outcome_rule.baseline_preservation: Do not rewrite the stage-47 baseline, native identifiability files, protocols, reports, figures or Word documents

output_rule.word: papers/前沿共生ENSO条件周期切片界_图文完整版.docx

prohibitions: No refitting, changed centers, covariance matrices, folds, periods or post-hoc candidate directions
No substitution of the marginal coefficient covariance block for the Schur-complement slice matrix
No calling fixed-period joint coefficient support a full-ellipsoid joint nonlinear optimum
No hiding of candidate violations or treating zero candidate violations as a global safety proof
No probability, confidence, posterior, calibrated-coverage or physical-period claim
No replacement of the stage-47 independent full-ellipsoid baseline by the conditional slice envelope
No exact rational-certificate claim for high-precision numerical intervals
No rewriting of historical files or use of center consistency as external scientific validation
